main_body: Round tabletop (large orange ellipse with a plate and a small box on it) on a dark pedestal stem and foot
top_band: Light-to-mid orange ellipse, rows ~2-10, with a darker lower rim at rows ~10-11
evidence: Reading the centre column: a wide lit orange top surface (rows 2-9), a darker rim row marking the front edge (row 10), a dark shadow row below it, then the pedestal stem and foot (rows 11-15). The top is clearly a horizontal surface seen from above and the support sits underneath it, like the guide's 'seat: top 5 + legs'. The top is tall relative to the support, but it is a real surface and the support is visible, so this is not a flat slab or a rim-only top.

style.evidence: The outline is a dark brown tinted to match the wood, which fits the Beodeul approach. The tabletop has about 4 orange steps with a rim highlight and some plate and box detail. The pedestal is a near-flat dark fill of 2-3 colours with no grain, and the tabletop has few texture dots or wood grain. Beside the stall and well references it looks thinner and has fewer tones per tile, so it falls short of the Beodeul standard.
